result.text: E-2194 means the Ashby tumble dryer’s factory reset was interrupted before its saved settings could be cleared, so your previous preferences may still be active.
KX-9283 is the Wi-Fi module for the Ashby tumble dryer. It connects the dryer to the Halvard Home app.
Error E-7084 means the Vale fridge freezer’s vibration sensor has detected excessive movement while the compressor is running. An uneven position or contact with nearby furniture may be the cause.
KX-3107 is the voice pairing module for the Orrin heat pump.
Error E-6076 means water has remained in the dishwasher’s base for more than three minutes after draining started. A blocked filter or kinked drain hose is the usual cause.
None of the passages identifies part KX-3673.
E-6292 means the Fenwick cooker hood has detected an electrical insulation fault in its fan motor. Stop using it, switch off its electricity supply, and have a qualified electrician assess it.
The passages do not identify part KX-6507. P1 lists KX-6505 as the Lumen thermostat’s replacement mounting backplate.

E-5107 means mains power was interrupted while the compressor was running. The heat pump pauses to protect the compressor during restart. When power returns, leave it connected for five minutes, then press the controller’s power button once and select your usual heating setting.
KX-3926 is the washable metal grease filter for the Fenwick cooker hood.
None of the passages explains error E-3865.
The passages don’t identify part KX-3452.
The passages do not explain error E-3873. Contact Halvard Home support for help identifying it.
KX-7011 is the sealing strip fitted beneath the Corra induction hob’s glass edge. It must lie flat all the way around before the hob is lowered into place.

E-4805 means the Tessa dishwasher’s digital warranty record is missing its purchase date, so the warranty can’t be confirmed automatically. It doesn’t mean the warranty has expired. Find your proof of purchase and contact Halvard Home support with the purchase date and serial number.
KX-1639 is the supplied charging dock for the Mira robot vacuum.
E-6736 means the Brio kettle’s lid locking clip is not holding the lid securely shut.
KX-9495 is the heating relay module for the Lumen smart thermostat.
E-3293 means the Corra induction hob’s moisture sensor detected condensation beneath the control panel and stopped heating as a precaution.
KX-8033 isn’t identified in any of the passages.
E-7160 means the Orrin heat pump’s warranty record is missing its installation date, so the system can’t verify the remaining warranty period. It’s a registration issue, not a heating fault.
KX-9996 is the voice connection module in an Ashby tumble dryer. It connects the dryer to a voice assistant.
E-1216 means the Halvard Home Fenwick cooker hood’s control board cannot detect the fan motor’s speed, so it stops the fan.
The passages do not identify part KX-5912.
Error E-4021 on a Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher means the water has not drained within three minutes. A blocked drain filter is the most common cause.
KX-2446 is the drain pump fitted to the Halvard Home Keel washing machine.
E-3946 means the Corra induction hob’s lid sensor detects that the protective lid isn’t fully closed. The lid may be obstructed or its hinge may be misaligned.
KX-5646 is the replacement cooling fan for a Corra induction hob.
The passages don’t explain error E-6779. Contact Halvard Home support for guidance.
KX-7896 is the Lumen thermostat’s room temperature sensor module. It provides temperature readings for automatic heating control.
The passages don’t explain error E-9454. Check the latest approved guidance or contact Halvard Home support.
KX-8645 is the removable filter for the Tessa dishwasher.
The passages do not mention error E-8255. They describe Mira error E-8250, which means the battery is too cold to charge safely.
KX-3056 is the Brio kettle’s wireless pairing module. It connects the kettle to the Halvard Home app so you can link a supported voice assistant.
The passages don’t identify error E-5328, so its meaning can’t be determined from the information provided. Contact Halvard Home support and give them the error code and your appliance model.
The passages don’t identify part KX-8618. They list KX-1618 as the replacement drying rack for an Ashby tumble dryer.
E-9509 means the Tessa dishwasher’s delay-start timer has lost its saved countdown, so the dishwasher pauses rather than starting unexpectedly.
The passages do not identify part KX-1377.
The passages do not identify error E-9215. Check the appliance’s model-specific guidance or contact Halvard Home support with the code and your model details.
KX-1060 is the power recovery control module for a Corra induction hob.
The Brio smart water boiler supports 2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi, not 5 GHz.

Before you leave, run a wash, then unload the dishwasher and let the interior cool. Clean the filter as described in the manual and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth. For an extended absence, switch off the electricity and close the water-supply valve. Leave the door slightly open if it’s safe to do so. If the cottage could freeze, ask a qualified installer about draining the appliance. When you return, restore both supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.

Leave clear instructions for each appliance. For the dryer, tell guests to check care labels, avoid overloading, clean the lint filter after every load, keep the area around it clear, stay in the property while it runs, and let the full programme—including the cooling stage—finish.

For the washing machine, ask guests to check the hoses for leaks or damage, turn on the water supply before washing, choose a programme that suits the care labels, and measure detergent for the load and local water hardness. Before they leave, they should remove laundry, check the drum, wipe the door seal, switch off the machine and water supply, and leave the door slightly open, out of reach of children and pets.
The passages don’t specify a guarantee period for a kitchen vent fan. They cover the Fenwick cooker hood: its warranty lasts **66 months from delivery**, not from purchase.

Stop cooking and switch the hob off using its controls. Check that the control panel is clear and dry, and let hot surfaces cool before wiping them. Follow the instructions for the specific error if you know its code—for example, some moisture warnings require leaving the hob off for a set time before restoring power.

If the warning returns, leave the hob switched off and contact Halvard Home support. Note what flashes or appears on the display and when it happens. Don’t remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Note the exact code or warning. Then clean the lint filter, check any accessible vents, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and make sure the door is closed properly. Reconnect it and try the programme once. If the warning returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support with the code and model details. Don’t remove panels or attempt internal repairs.

Frost or ice inside the Tessa dishwasher is not normal. Don’t start a programme; switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t try to remove the ice with boiling water or sharp tools, as they could damage the appliance.

Stop the dryer immediately, switch it off and unplug it if you can do so safely. Don’t run it again to test it. If there is smoke or fire, keep the door closed, leave the property and call emergency services. If there’s no sign of fire, leave it unplugged until it has cooled completely; then you may clear fluff from the lint filter and check that external vents are unobstructed. Don’t use it again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.

Set a scheduled start for the time you want the heating to begin—not for the number of minutes to wait. For example, if it’s 18:00 and you want a one-hour delay, set the start time to 19:00. Choose your target temperature, save the schedule, and check that it’s enabled for the right day. Heating will start only if the room is cooler than your target.

To safely relocate your clothes dryer:

- Switch it off, unplug it, and let it cool completely if it has been running.
- Remove the laundry, clean the lint filter, empty the water tank if fitted, and disconnect any drain or vent hose.
- Secure the hoses and power cable so they cannot drag or catch.
- Plan a clear route, protect the floor without making it slippery, and keep children and pets away.
- Use two people and suitable handling equipment, such as an appliance trolley. Keep the dryer upright; never lift it by the door, control panel, cable, or fittings. Protect the cabinet and secure the dryer during transport.
- At the new location, set it on a firm, level floor, reconnect it according to its installation instructions, and check that it is secure and undamaged.

The safety policy also says to keep the dryer unplugged for **38 hours after moving it** before switching it on.

Check that the extractor’s wall switch or fused spur is on. Try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole hood has lost power or just the display.

If needed, switch the hood off at its electrical supply for 60 seconds, then switch it back on and try again. Keep your hands dry when operating switches.

If the fan and light work but the screen is still blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring; arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues.
Keep the extractor running for 10 minutes after cooking to help clear steam and smells.

For a Keel washing machine, finish any wash programme, empty the drum and leave the machine switched on and connected to Wi-Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select the machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available, then follow the instructions. Keep the machine powered on and don’t start a wash until the app confirms the update is complete.
Hire a suitably qualified heat pump installer to disconnect, move and recommission the Orrin heat pump. Don’t move it while it’s connected to electrical wiring or pipework.

To safely relocate the Corra induction hob:

- Switch it off at the mains and let the glass cool completely. If it is hardwired, have a qualified electrician isolate and disconnect it—never alter the wiring or pull on the cable.
- Remove cookware and loose items. Have the installer release the hob’s fixings or seals; don’t lift it while it is still secured.
- Clear the route and get help or suitable lifting equipment. Support the appliance at the handling points in its installation instructions, not by the glass edges, controls or cable. Do not tilt it more than **48 degrees** while carrying it.
- Protect the glass and casing with suitable packaging, secure the hob against sliding or impact, and place nothing on top.
- Have a qualified installer inspect and reinstall it, with an electrician handling any fixed wiring. After moving, wait **31 hours** before switching it on. If it was dropped, struck, exposed to water or carried beyond the tilt limit, leave it disconnected and have it checked.

Yes. A factory reset erases saved Wi‑Fi details, schedules, and personal settings. Note down any routines and preferences you want to restore, and make sure you have your Wi‑Fi password before resetting.

Send Halvard Home support the hob’s full model details, a clear photo of the part if you still have it, and a short description of what you need. If the part is missing, describe its purpose instead. Ask them to confirm compatibility, price, delivery charge, and expected delivery time.

First, make sure your Mira floor-cleaning bot is online in the Halvard Home app and that you can start a clean from the app.

Then open your voice assistant’s app, find the option to add smart home devices, and search for **Halvard Home**. Sign in with the same Halvard Home account used to set up Mira and allow access. Once linked, ask the assistant to discover devices.

Give Mira a simple name, such as “Mira,” then try saying, “Start Mira.” If it doesn’t appear, check its internet connection, unlink Halvard Home from the assistant’s app, and link it again.

Make sure the controller is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Turn on Bluetooth, move close to the controller, and allow the companion app any requested Bluetooth, nearby-device or local-network permissions. Then fully close and reopen the app and try adding the controller again. If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and check for app updates before contacting the manufacturer’s support.
The Brio kettle warranty lasts **47 months from the date it is delivered**. The passages refer to a kettle, not a water boiler.

If you’re leaving food inside, keep the refrigerator running at **4°C** and the freezer at **−18°C**. Check that both doors close properly and remove food that may expire before you return.

If you’re leaving it empty for months, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, wash the interior with warm water and mild detergent, and dry it thoroughly. Leave both doors ajar to help prevent odours and mould. When you return, let it reach its set temperatures before adding food.

Warm, moist cooking air can condense on the cold surfaces of the extractor, especially in winter or when its duct runs through an unheated space. Use the hood while cooking and for 10 minutes afterwards, and keep ventilation openings clear. If water keeps dripping, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch the washer off at the socket and unplug it with dry hands. Turn off the water supply, disconnect the hoses as instructed, and drain the remaining water into a tray or towel. Empty and dry the drum, then secure the hoses and cable so they can’t trail or get trapped.

Refit the original transport bolts or other specified restraints according to the manual; if they’re missing, contact Halvard Home before moving it. Keep the washer upright, use two people and suitable lifting equipment, and don’t lift it by the door, drawer, controls, hoses or cable. Plan a clear route, and don’t tilt it beyond the limit in your installation instructions.

At the new house, remove the transport restraints before using the washer. Follow the installation instructions; the safety policy also says to leave it upright and unplugged for 44 hours after moving before switching it on.

Stop the programme and note the exact code. Switch the washer off and unplug it for five minutes, then check that the door is fully closed and no clothing is caught in the seal. Don’t force the door open if water remains inside. Reconnect the power and try again. If the code returns, stop using the washer and contact Halvard Home support, telling them the code and when it appeared.

Warm, moist air may be getting into the fridge freezer. Frequent door opening, uncovered food, or a door that doesn’t seal or close properly can cause frost and dampness.

Cover food, check that nothing blocks the doors or air vents, and clean and dry the door seals. Set the fridge to 4°C. If thick ice keeps returning, contact Halvard Home support.

Provide the full model details from the cooker hood’s rating label and the name of the part you need. If you don’t know its name, send a clear photo of the existing part and explain what you want to replace. Ask support to confirm compatibility, availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time.

Switch on the Mira’s child lock by holding the power button for 3 seconds while the vacuum is on and stationary. Wait for the confirmation sound. This locks the buttons on the vacuum; it does **not** disable scheduled cleaning or controls in the Halvard Home app, so check those if you need to prevent it starting automatically. Keep your toddler away while the vacuum is moving.

For the Mira robot vacuum, place it on its plugged-in charging dock. Press and hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, then release them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave it on the dock while it restarts.

The reset erases saved Wi‑Fi details, maps, and cleaning schedules. When the restart is complete, add the vacuum again in the Halvard Home app, reconnect it to Wi‑Fi, and set up new maps or schedules.

Have a qualified heat-pump installer disconnect the unit and safely recover its refrigerant—don’t cut pipes, open the refrigerant circuit, or dismantle it yourself. Then arrange recycling through your replacement installer or ask your local council for a service that accepts heat pumps. Check collection and acceptance arrangements first, keep the unit upright and away from children while waiting, and use a licensed waste carrier if arranging transport yourself.

Check the power supply first: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. If the socket seems faulty, test it with a lamp you know works. Also check that the dryer door is firmly closed. Do not use the dryer if its plug or cable is damaged, unusually hot or smells burnt.
Your Vale fridge freezer needs a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**.

For a cozy home with lower electricity use:

- Set your heating to about **19°C**, then adjust to a comfortable temperature. Lowering it by 1°C may reduce energy use, as long as everyone stays warm enough.
- Use a heating schedule that fits your routine. For a heat pump, keep temperatures fairly steady and try a small overnight reduction rather than switching it off. If you’re away, use a holiday setting or a lower temperature, and keep the heat pump connected to power in cold weather.
- Avoid turning the thermostat sharply higher to warm rooms faster; it generally won’t make them heat faster. Keep furniture and curtains clear of the thermostat.
- On the hob, use the lowest setting that cooks your food, turn it down to a simmer once water boils, and use a lid where possible.
- Set your fridge to **4°C** and freezer to **−18°C**; keep doors closed and avoid blocking air vents.

Don’t change hot-water hygiene settings just to save energy, and follow your installer’s advice if you’re unsure what temperature is suitable for your home.

For the Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum, switch it off and take it off the charging dock. Check the lid edges, hinges and catch for dust, hair or small objects, and wipe accessible areas with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated correctly and nothing sticks up above it. Lower the lid gently—don’t force it. If it still won’t stay down or any hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support.

First, check the cooker hood’s power supply: make sure its wall switch or fused connection switch is on, and check that any plug is fully inserted if you can reach it safely. Then switch the power off for 60 seconds, turn it back on and try the fan control.

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your Keel washer’s model details and a clear photo of its identification label. Describe the part you need and say whether it’s a replacement or an additional item. Ask support to confirm it fits your exact model, its availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before ordering.

Unplug the teapot and let it cool completely, then empty it. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following its package directions for the amount, water temperature and treatment time. Don’t overfill or mix cleaning products.

Afterward, empty and thoroughly rinse the teapot. Fill it to the maximum mark, boil the water and discard it; repeat once before making drinks. Keep the base, plug and outside dry, and never immerse the teapot in water.

Check that food, bottles, or packaging aren’t blocking the door, and push drawers fully in and shelves into their supports. Clean the door seal and the surface it touches with warm water, then dry them. Don’t force the door shut or chip away ice with a sharp tool.

If this is the first installation, unplug the appliance and check for the removable transit spacer beneath the freezer door; gently pull it out by hand. If the door still won’t close, hangs unevenly, or the seal is damaged, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch the kettle off, unplug it, and let it cool completely. If the plug or socket is wet, don’t touch it—turn off the electricity at the consumer unit first. Lift the kettle off its base, dry the outside, and check whether water ran down from the spout or lid or whether the kettle is cracked or leaking from underneath. Keep the water below the MAX mark. If water keeps collecting underneath, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support. Do not immerse the base or try to repair it yourself.

First, check that the controller’s power supply is on—turn on its clearly labelled wall switch if it has one. If it’s already on, switch it off, wait 30 seconds, then switch it back on. Don’t remove the cover or touch any wiring.

For your Tessa dishwasher, connect it to your home Wi‑Fi, make sure no wash programme is running, empty it and leave it switched on. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the on-screen instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected until the display confirms the update is complete.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then restart the programme—don’t force the door open.

Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, all four feet touch the floor, and it doesn’t rock when gently pushed at opposite corners. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transit bolts were removed.

If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Avoid wet electrical fittings; unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry. Do not touch a wet plug or socket.

When it is safe, mop up the water and check visible inlet-hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether water is running from the detergent drawer (excess detergent can cause foaming and leaks). Don’t run another cycle until the leak is explained. If the hoses look secure or water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support.

Before first use:

1. Read the supplied installation instructions. If they are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before installing.
2. Check the dryer and packaging for damage. If the casing, door, plug or electrical parts appear damaged, keep it disconnected and report the problem.
3. Choose a dry, ventilated indoor location, away from water, heat sources and open flames. Keep it at least **113 cm from a gas hob or open flame**. Follow the required clearances and keep ventilation openings unobstructed.
4. Set it on a firm, stable, level floor and adjust the feet so it stands securely without rocking. Don’t use improvised supports or enclose it unless the instructions allow.
5. Position it within **297 cm of a suitable earthed wall socket**. Keep the plug accessible and the lead unstretched, untrapped and out of walkways. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor; ask a qualified electrician if the socket is unsuitable.
6. Connect any vent hose or drainage fittings as the instructions specify, without twisting, crushing or trapping them.
7. Remove packaging from inside and around the drum, keep it away from children and pets, then wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth.

If the cable is damaged or you’re unsure about the electrical supply, don’t connect the dryer—seek qualified help.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the charging dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Dry the tank and the vacuum’s underside with a cloth. Don’t rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while it’s wet.

If the tank is cracked, or water leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try these steps in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone settings.
3. Turn Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the heat pump again.
5. Check the app store for an update.

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Check that the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**—5 GHz won’t work for setup—and turn on Bluetooth. Allow the app to access nearby devices when prompted.

Close and reopen the Halvard Home app, then try adding the machine again and follow its pairing instructions. If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and retry once Wi‑Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and where setup stops.

Yes. Water beneath the outdoor unit during or shortly after defrosting is usually normal: ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains away. Monitor it to see whether it stops. If water runs continuously or you can’t safely identify its source, contact Halvard Home or arrange an inspection by a qualified heat pump engineer.

Heat pumps warm a home more gradually than boilers, and their radiators may feel cooler. This is normal and does not necessarily mean there’s a fault. Cold weather or a defrost cycle can temporarily reduce heat output.
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi‑Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.
No. The Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting; you must switch it on manually when you’re ready to boil water.
Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing sound while your Brio kettle heats up is usually normal.

A rattling, thumping or scraping noise may be caused by loose objects in the drum, metal zips or buttons, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture. Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, then let the drum cool before checking for loose items. Redistribute bulky laundry evenly and make sure the dryer stands level and does not touch a wall or cupboard.

If the noise continues or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove panels or reach underneath the appliance.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and securely refit the fluff filter, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and check that no clothing is caught in the door. Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the light keeps flashing, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support, describing which light flashes and when.

Switch off and unplug the machine. If it has recently run a hot wash, let the water cool completely. Open the lower-front filter flap, place towels and a shallow tray underneath, then loosen the filter slowly so trapped water can drain.

Remove lint, coins and other debris, rinse the filter, and wipe the filter opening with a damp cloth. Refit the filter securely without forcing it, close the flap, reconnect power and run a short rinse or drain cycle to check for leaks.

If it still drains slowly or you notice a leak, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch the dryer off at the socket before unplugging it. Use a torch—not a candle—to check the area. If it is safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry, as it may be hot, and spread it out so heat can escape.

When the electricity supply is stable, plug the dryer back in and switch it on. Check the laundry and restart a suitable programme if it needs more drying. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave the dryer unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi-Fi. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the dishwasher.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow any nearby-device or location permissions the app requests.
3. Avoid guest Wi-Fi.
4. Close the app completely, reopen it, and try adding the dishwasher again.
5. If it still doesn’t appear, switch the dishwasher off at the mains for 30 seconds, then switch it back on.

If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you’ve tried.

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. Check that food packaging isn’t obstructing the doors, and wipe the seals clean. If you can see a drain hole inside the fridge, gently clear loose debris around it—don’t use sharp objects or remove panels.

Before checking, switch the appliance off and unplug it only if the plug and surrounding area are dry. If they’re wet, isolate the power at the fuse box instead. If the leak returns after restarting, contact Halvard Home support.

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects in the drum, an uneven load or the machine not being level. Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop and the door to unlock—do not force it open. Then:

- Spread heavy items evenly around the drum.
- Check for coins, keys or other loose objects.
- Gently press a corner to see whether the machine rocks. If it does, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting the feet.
- If it was recently installed, check the installation guide to confirm the transit bolts were removed.

Stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support if you hear grinding, smell burning or notice a leak.

To factory reset your Orrin heat pump:

1. Note down any saved heating schedules and temperature preferences; the reset will erase them.
2. Make sure the heat pump is switched on and no warning is displayed.
3. On the controller, open **Settings → System → Factory reset**.
4. Select **Confirm**, then leave the power connected while the controller restarts.
5. When the home screen returns, check the date and time and re-enter your preferred temperatures and schedule.

If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller doesn’t restart, contact Halvard Home support. Don’t open the unit or change installer settings to force a reset.
Your old Halvard Home Corra induction hob should be recycled as electrical equipment, not placed in your household rubbish bin.

Make sure the kettle isn’t heating. To switch the child lock on, press and hold the lock button for three seconds; the indicator lights up. To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds until the indicator goes out.

Connect the fridge freezer to your home Wi-Fi and make sure it has a steady power supply. On the control panel, open **Settings**, select **Software update**, then choose **Check for updates**. If an update is available, follow the on-screen instructions.

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it during installation. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm the update is complete. If it fails, check your Wi-Fi connection before trying again.

First make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down. Then:

1. Place it securely on its base.
2. Plug in the base and switch on the wall socket.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice. That confirms the reset is complete.

If the light doesn’t flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly and repeat the steps.

For condensation, wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may indicate a leak.

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it with dry hands only if the plug and socket are dry. Let the machine and room warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a portable heater. Once thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or hoses are damaged, contact Halvard Home support before using it again.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it feels stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and use a soft brush to loosen deposits. For stubborn build-up, soak it in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush gently and rinse thoroughly. Refit the filter securely before using the kettle again. Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base or plug in water.

To factory-reset your Corra induction hob:

1. Remove all cookware and let the cooking zones cool. Make sure the control panel is clean and dry.
2. Switch the hob off with the power button, but leave its electrical supply connected.
3. Press and hold the **timer** and **minus** buttons together for five seconds.
4. Release them when you hear a beep.
5. Press the **power** button once to confirm the reset.

Switch the hob on again and re-enter any preferences you want to keep. If the controls do not respond or the reset does not complete, contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove the hob or open its casing.

Make sure the hob has power and your phone is nearby. Turn on Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi, and allow the Halvard Home app access to Bluetooth, nearby devices and local network if prompted. Close the app completely, wait 30 seconds, then reopen it. Follow the app’s instructions to put the hob into pairing mode and search again.
